name: ParkSim-VLA-Bench-v0
description: Reproducible high-level policy benchmark for ParkSim Qwen-VLA and deterministic baselines.
notes: All agents share the same lower-level A*/Stanley/parking executor unless the agent is the original rule_based controller.
Qwen-VLA must choose an action_id from valid_actions; safety shield rejects malformed or unsafe choices.
Preference pairs are derived from completed/path/time/shield/fallback objective scores and are intended for prompt optimization or offline preference tuning.
Benchmark validation fails on empty or structurally incomplete episode logs so paper tables do not include partial runs.
Safety metrics are computed from synchronized ego/background traces and decision logs, including near-miss, collision-proxy, TTC, and unsafe occupancy choices.
Visualizer video artifacts should be paired with video_manifest.json to bind videos, frame counts, simulation-time alignment, and metrics.
Controlled ego vehicles block the entrance spawn gate by default, so random entering vehicles wait until the ego leaves the entrance region instead of spawning on top of it.
Use python -m parksim.vla.paper_report to aggregate multiple validated benchmark directories into mean/std/95CI tables and paired deltas against a reference agent.
Paper reports also export paired sign tests, Wilcoxon signed-rank normal approximations, paired effect sizes, scenario-factor stratification, and a reproducibility manifest for method replication.
Use python -m parksim.vla.paper_gate to distinguish pilot-complete suites from paper-ready suites and to export actionable missing-coverage checks.
Cross-vehicle safety metrics synchronize traces by wall_time when available; per-vehicle relative time is used only as a fallback.
Use scripts/run_vla_paper_suite.sh for paper-scale orchestration across background modes, density levels, seeds, and agents.
The suite runner delegates each condition to run_vla_benchmark.sh, validates each benchmark directory, and then calls parksim.vla.paper_report for final tables.
Paper-suite replay mode skips non-empty density configs by default because replay ignores random entering/exiting spawn density.
Paper-suite runs support resume-by-validation, dry-run planning, and continue-on-fail failure recording.
Suite manifests include per-condition status values such as planned, completed, skipped_valid, and failed.
Each Qwen-VLA decision log stores the versioned decision_packet seen by the policy, including valid_action_ids, valid_actions, hard constraints, and BEV attachment metadata.
The safety shield rejects a decision when target_spot_index is inconsistent with the selected action_id, even if action_id itself is valid.
Protocol compliance metrics include target_mismatch_decision_count and missing_reason_code_count in addition to malformed_decision_count and shield_rejection_count.

Use python -m parksim.vla.decision_audit to audit decision logs for protocol version, prompt version, valid action membership, target consistency, reason codes, shield rejections, and unsafe applied spots.
Decision audit failures are exported as JSONL so paper experiments can index and replay representative Qwen-VLA failure cases.
Paper-suite real Qwen mode starts one managed Qwen service per suite and passes its endpoint to child benchmarks as external to avoid repeated model reloads.
Suite manifests record qwen.mode, qwen.bench_mode, qwen.managed, qwen.ready, endpoint, health payload, and service-log presence.

Cloud-fleet experiments use a two-phase decision barrier: the simulator confirms a frozen epoch before context collection, and every addressed AV confirms action application at the same simulation time before advancement resumes.
Qwen wall-clock response time is retained only in raw JSONL for engineering audit and is excluded from performance metrics and statistical comparisons.
VLA baseline agents share the same valid action bundle interface as Qwen-VLA so comparisons isolate high-level selection rather than low-level control.
Bundle-aware baselines evaluate executable spot-route-wait candidates using route length, expected wait, dynamic conflict risk, and conflicting vehicle count.
Entry parking tasks do not expose cruise_to_exit as a valid action; exit actions are generated only for exiting or UNPARK task semantics.
Reservation_bundle approximates time-window reservation by penalizing expected wait, path conflict risk, and conflicting vehicle count on each executable spot-route-wait bundle.
Centralized_min_cost is a deterministic centralized-cost proxy over the same candidate bundle set; it uses global occupancy, nearby-traffic load, and path-conflict terms without using an LLM.
Oracle_intent_bundle reveals background task/progress/reference-path information and is treated as an upper-bound baseline, not as a deployable partially observable policy.

No LoRA, DPO, or model weight adaptation is part of this protocol; Qwen-VLA optimization is restricted to decision packet design, constrained action bundles, safety shielding, and prompt-level selection objectives.

Replay vehicle IDs are reserved before any controlled or scheduled vehicle is launched; dynamic IDs are allocated above the complete replay-ID range to keep ROS namespaces and trace files globally unique.

Benchmark validation rejects any trace with identity changes, relative-time regression, wall-time regression, or physically implausible position jumps; invalid traces are excluded from paper evidence.
